messages:
incident-bot: alert - Elevated 5xx rate detected for /v1/generate (prod, cluster-us-east-1)
incident-bot: symptom: gateway timeouts and 502 spikes from gateway pool -> 12% error rate over last 2m :rotating_light:
incident-bot: paging: oncall emma@redwood (pager duty)

emma: on it. joining channel. initial hypothesis: batcher backlog -> HOL blocking. pulling metrics now.

javier: I see long tail in batch queue age and a steady increase in queued requests on scheduler-batcher-3. avg enqueue_time 700ms -> 5s the last 10m.
li: runtime traces show repeated cache miss + KV lookup spikes on host gpu-12, some requests hitting remote K/V store and waiting ~1.2s each, causing batch windows to stretch.

mina: customer impacts: two enterprise customers reported UI stalls and increased latencies on chat endpoints. support ticket IDs: #3482, #3483.

emma: ok immediate mitigation steps: 1) stop routing new traffic to scheduler-batcher-3, 2) enable emergency eviction on the busiest batchers, 3) fallback route to smaller model variant. can someone run the commands?

javier: running drain on scheduler-batcher-3 now (evict policy: oldest-first).
```bash
# drain commands
./infractl scheduler drain --cluster=us-east-1 --node=scheduler-batcher-3 --evict-policy=oldest-first
```

deploy-bot: deploy triggered: route-fallback v1.2 -> v1.1 (smaller model) across gateways us-east-1; rollout in progress.

li: enabling eviction flags on batcher runtime, toggling immediate-eviction=true
```yaml
runtime.batch.eviction: immediate-eviction: true
runtime.batch.max_window_ms: 80
```

emma: scaling note: spin up two extra batcher replicas on warm-pool so we have spare capacity if drain doesn't clear backlog. javier can you request capacity?

javier: requested extra batchers, autoscaler acknowledged. provisioning started.

mina: customers notified with brief status update: "We are mitigating an infrastructure issue impacting short-term request timeouts for some endpoints. Engineers are actively routing traffic and performing live mitigations. We'll update in 30 minutes."

paul: logs from gateway showing 502s:
```text
[2026-03-15T19:02:11Z] gateway-7 | upstream timeout when proxying to scheduler-batcher-3
[2026-03-15T19:02:12Z] gateway-7 | 502 response to client id=acct-9921
```

li: digging into runtime: kv client had an intermittent spike of connection resets to KVS cluster -> ~40% of requests in long-tail attempted remote KV. We're going to enable local cache bypass heuristics (serve-stale) to reduce round trips.

emma: good. also throttle long-running requests at the gateway to avoid HOL blocking other short requests. set per-route max-inflight=20 and max-queue-ms=2000.

javier: applied gateway rate limits, verifying metrics. we see queue depth on scheduler-batcher-3 drop by ~30% in 2m. 5xx rate trending down.

deploy-bot: route fallback completed to v1.1 -> 100% for affected route in us-east-1.

mina: support: customers on premium tiers still seeing intermittent errors but far fewer. continuing to monitor.

emma: handoff prep: I'll stay on for the next 30m and then pass to javier for the longer remediation window. checklist for handoff: 1) confirm backlog drained to <50 requests per node, 2) eviction flag persisted, 3) KV cluster incident ticket opened (#KVS-987), 4) postmortem draft assigned.

javier: noted. I'll own remediation and root cause analysis. immediate followups: dig into KV connection pool config, add circuit breaker to KV client, and add health check to detect batch window elongation.

li: adding guards in runtime: avoid remote KV synchronous fetch in critical hot paths, add async refresh + stale fallback. pushing patch to canary.

emma: final state at handoff time: 5xx rate down to 1.2%, average p95 latency from 1.8s -> 420ms, backlog across batchers returned to normal.

paul: handoff summary posted to incident channel and ops log. tagging this thread for postmortem.

emma: thanks all. creating incident ticket INC-2026-032 with timeline and attachments. will follow up with customer impact summary and postmortem draft. :white_check_mark:
